change_interpretations.engineering_summary: Requirement VCU-MOD-06 defining Comfort and Sport driver operating modes and torque ramp profiles has been removed from the specification. Verification of mode-specific torque ramps is no longer required.

assessments.reason: This test verifies accelerator step response latency against VCU-DR-01, which remains unchanged. It does not exercise the removed operating mode feature VCU-MOD-06.
evidence: Procedure checks 100 ms threshold for pedal step response
assessments.recommended_action: Retain existing test procedure and baseline.

assessments.reason: This test checks brake override priority over pedal demand under VCU-DR-01 and VCU-BRK-03, both of which are unchanged.
evidence: Procedure checks emergency brake override priority
assessments.recommended_action: Retain test in the verification suite without changes.

assessments.reason: Traceability is broken due to a missing requirement link following migration. Human review is required to restore the requirement link and verify whether torque transients relate to any changed functionality.
evidence: Workshop note: High-load campaign did not keep all requirement hyperlinks after migration
assessments.recommended_action: Reconcile requirement link with the system engineer to restore traceability.

assessments.reason: The test verifies emergency brake actuator latency under VCU-BRK-03, which is unchanged. Note that per workshop notes, brake latency uses a different clock than torque latency.
evidence: Workshop note: Brake command latency and positive torque command latency use different clocks

assessments.reason: The test verifies wheel-speed sensor degradation behavior under VCU-DGN-04, an unchanged requirement.
evidence: Procedure checks degraded mode and fault log upon sensor unplug
assessments.recommended_action: Maintain test case in regression suite.

assessments.reason: The test procedure relies on switching between Comfort and Sport modes to check audit trail logging under VCU-LOG-05. Since VCU-MOD-06 was removed, the mode selection stimulus specified in the procedure may no longer exist or operate as intended.
evidence: Procedure: Change Comfort to Sport; log timestamp and build identifier
assessments.recommended_action: Re-check test procedure stimulus with system engineer to align mode transitions with current system architecture.

assessments.reason: Traceability and ownership are unconfirmed because the requirement link is marked TBD and the test has not been run.
evidence: Comment: Ownership and source link to be clarified
assessments.recommended_action: Clarify requirement linkage and test ownership with team lead.

assessments.reason: Traceability is broken because the test links to an unknown legacy requirement ID VCU-OLD-88.
evidence: Comment: Imported row; requirements catalog changed
assessments.recommended_action: Map legacy test to current active requirements catalog or archive if obsolete.

assessments.reason: The test directly evaluates Sport vs Comfort torque ramp profiles for VCU-MOD-06, which has been removed from the specification. The test procedure and verification purpose are invalidated by the requirement removal.
evidence: Procedure: Compare accelerator response under Sport vs Comfort during ramp and release
assessments.recommended_action: Decommission or update test TV-009 following the removal of VCU-MOD-06.

assessments.reason: The test verifies pedal transient spike filtering under VCU-DR-02, an unchanged requirement.
evidence: Procedure injects 7 ms pulse to test pedal signal validation
assessments.recommended_action: Retain test procedure and execution script.

assessments.reason: The test evaluates positive torque cancellation during emergency braking under VCU-BRK-03, which remains unchanged.
evidence: Procedure verifies torque drop upon emergency brake request

assessments.reason: Traceability is broken as the requirement reference link is missing from the register.
evidence: Procedure checks ECU power cycle readiness within 500 ms
assessments.recommended_action: Assign formal requirement link for ECU wake-up timing.
